pr.title: [4.x] Restore existing attributes and classes after wire:loading
pr.source: PR description, changed browser tests, production code, and observed behavior

evidence.assertion: Existing DOM state survives one continuous loading period.
evidence.explanation: All four focused regressions fail. In the playground, the fast request finishes while the slow request is still pending, but the target becomes enabled and loses its existing class.
evidence.output:
Exit 1 · 4 tests, 10 assertions, 4 failures
Attribute restoration: disabled became false
Class restoration: existing class disappeared
Overlap + delay: disabled disappeared before the slow request finished

evidence.assertion: Existing DOM state survives one continuous loading period.
evidence.explanation: The submitted PR keeps loading active through the final overlapping request, then restores the exact attribute and class state captured at the start.
evidence.output:
Exit 0 · 4 tests, 17 assertions · PASS
Playground after fast request: disabled=true, classes=target existing loading-added
Playground after slow request: disabled=false, classes=target existing

evidence.assertion: Existing DOM state survives one continuous loading period.
evidence.explanation: Two independently ordered causal steps reproduce the submitted production fix exactly and pass the same executable evidence.
evidence.output:
Exit 0 · 4 tests, 17 assertions · PASS
JavaScript suite: 110 passed, 1 skipped
Production comparison with Original: identical

environments.label: Before
environments.description: Merge base with submitted regression tests overlaid

environments.label: Reconstruction
environments.description: Merge base plus two causal commits

stories.title: Restore what existed before loading began
stories.what_was_wrong: Cleanup always applied the inverse loading operation. It removed attributes and classes even when Alpine or the server-rendered DOM had already put them there.
stories.what_changed: The first loading start snapshots the named attribute value and each named class membership, then cleanup restores that exact snapshot.
stories.why_necessary: A renderless action has no later morph to repair DOM state that loading cleanup destroyed.
stories.proof: The two renderless attribute/class regressions fail Before and pass in Original and Reconstruction.

stories.title: Treat overlap as one loading period
stories.what_was_wrong: Each request independently ended loading, so the first completed request could restore the target while another request was still active. Delayed loading made the race easier to expose.
stories.what_changed: A local active count captures and starts loading only on the first request, then restores only after the final request finishes.
stories.why_necessary: The element owns one visible loading period, not one toggle lifecycle per transport request.
stories.proof: Both overlap regressions and the live playground keep the target disabled after Fast finishes and restore it only after Slow finishes.

diffs.label: Submitted PR · js/directives/wire-loading.js
diffs.patch:
diff --git a/js/directives/wire-loading.js b/js/directives/wire-loading.js
index daa4ee0e..dd18c6dd 100644
--- a/js/directives/wire-loading.js
+++ b/js/directives/wire-loading.js
@@ -10,14 +10,49 @@ directive('loading', ({ el, directive, component, cleanup }) => {
 
     let [delay, abortDelay] = applyDelay(directive)
 
+    let restoreLoadingState = () => toggleBooleanStateDirective(el, directive, false)
+    let activeLoadingCount = 0
+
+    let startLoading = () => {
+        if (activeLoadingCount === 0) {
+            if (directive.modifiers.includes('class')) {
+                let classes = directive.expression.split(' ').filter(String)
+                let classStates = classes.map(className => [className, el.classList.contains(className)])
+
+                restoreLoadingState = () => classStates.forEach(([className, wasPresent]) => {
+                    el.classList.toggle(className, wasPresent)
+                })
+            } else if (directive.modifiers.includes('attr')) {
+                let attribute = directive.expression
+                let value = el.getAttribute(attribute)
+
+                restoreLoadingState = value === null
+                    ? () => el.removeAttribute(attribute)
+                    : () => el.setAttribute(attribute, value)
+            }
+
+            delay(() => toggleBooleanStateDirective(el, directive, true))
+        }
+
+        activeLoadingCount++
+    }
+
+    let endLoading = () => {
+        if (activeLoadingCount === 0) return
+
+        activeLoadingCount--
+
+        if (activeLoadingCount === 0) abortDelay(restoreLoadingState)
+    }
+
     let cleanupA = whenTargetsArePartOfRequest(component, el, targets, inverted, [
-        () => delay(() => toggleBooleanStateDirective(el, directive, true)),
-        () => abortDelay(() => toggleBooleanStateDirective(el, directive, false)),
+        startLoading,
+        endLoading,
     ])
 
     let cleanupB = whenTargetsArePartOfFileUpload(component, targets, [
-        () => delay(() => toggleBooleanStateDirective(el, directive, true)),
-        () => abortDelay(() => toggleBooleanStateDirective(el, directive, false)),
+        startLoading,
+        endLoading,
     ])
 
     cleanup(() => {

learning_events.statement: For wire:loading, overlapping transport requests form one element-owned loading period; restore state only at the final completion.
